Proposition
[duality between closed forms and symmetric derivatives]

Source: petersen:page-0350, petersen:page-0351 ↗ def:pet-ch9-de-rham-cohomology ↗ def:pet-ch9-codifferential 1. ch9:9.2.1Let $ heta =X^ lat $, so $ heta (v)=g(v,X)$. Then

  1. the endomorphism $v\mapsto abla _vX$ is self-adjoint exactly when $ heta $ is closed;

  2. $\delta heta =-\operatorname {div}X$.

Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch9-vector-field-1form-duality \sketch The identity $d heta (V,W)+(\mathcal L_Xg)(V,W)=2g( abla _VX,W)$ separates the alternating and symmetric parts of $ abla X$, proving the first claim. Tracing the covariant derivative of the metric-dual relation gives $\delta heta =-\operatorname {div}X$.

□

Consequently, when $ heta $ is harmonic then $\operatorname {div}X=0$ and $ abla X$ is a symmetric $(1,1)$-tensor; the Bochner formula for closed $1$-forms is stated below through the dual vector field.
